To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the torA gene is located at 28.3 U on the E. coli chromosome, and that the TorA enzyme is a TMAO reductase.
a Mud1 insertion mutation of Escherichiacoli was obtained in which thelacstructural genes were fused to themajor structural gene of the TMAO reductase (torA).

a Mud1 insertion mutant in which the lacZ gene is fused to the promoter region of torA, encoding trimethylamine N-Oxide (TMAO)-reductase, is induced in the presence of TMAO and that the torA gene is different from any of the previously known tor genes in Escherichiacoli or in Salmonella Typhimurium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the regulation of the tor operon which encodes the structural genes for the TMAO reductase in E. coli. The
the regulation of the tor::Mudd operon fusion in E. coli.
the regulation of the Tor system in E. coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the torA gene encodes the TMAO reductase, that its expression is regulated in a manner similar to nar genes, and that it is not under the control of the nirR gene.

the Tor operon is not regulated by the same mechanisms as those controlling the Nar or Nir operons, and is independent of the NirR protein; it is not regulated by molybdenium; it is not a part of the pyrimidine biosynthetic pathway; it is probably a single operon.

torA is a TMAO reductase gene and that the torA::Mud1 gene fusion is an oxygen-repressible and TMAO-inducible operon which is not subject to the positive control by the nirR protein or the molybdate control mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regulation of torA is not as simple as that of narG.
the regulation of the tor operon is different from that of the nitrate reductive pathway, which is under the control of nirR and molybdenocofactor.
the tor::Mudd operon is regulated by TMAO, by oxygen and by the molybdopterin cofactor, in the same way as the nar::Mud1 and nar::Mud2 operons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the torA gene is not regulated in the same way as the other tor genes, which are under nirR and narL control.
the TMAO reductase is not a molybdopterin-containing enzyme.
the torA gene product, the trimethylamine oxide (TMAO), N-oxide reductase, is not regulated by the molybdopterin cofactor, as is nitrate reductases.
